prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a sideswipe while changing lanes in Pearland, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1282; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather just say I'm the driver of the vehicle involved. Go ahead and ask your questions.

Q: Understood. Can you tell me where the accident occurred?

A: It was on a multi-lane road in Pearland, Texas, near a shopping center entrance. I was in the right lane and wanted to move over to the left.

Q: What were you doing right before the collision?

A: I checked my mirror, signaled, and started to change lanes. I thought the lane was clear, but a vehicle came up on my left side and we sideswiped each other.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you moved over?

A: Honestly, no. I glanced at the mirror but I didn't see it until the impact. It was in my blind spot.

Q: Were you able to stop or steer away?

A: I tried to correct back into my lane, but there wasn't time. Both of our cars scraped along each other for a second or two before we stopped.

Q: Did you have any injuries at the scene?

A: I felt fine at first, just shaken up. But within a day my neck was really stiff and sore, and now I have headaches and pain between my shoulders. My doctor said it looks like whiplash.

Q: Have you received any medical treatment since the accident?

A: Yes, I've been going to physical therapy three times a week and I'm taking prescribed pain medication. I'm still having trouble turning my head to the left.

Q: Did anyone else in your vehicle get hurt?

A: No, I was alone in the car.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I want to be clear I didn't intend to cut anyone off. I just didn't see the other car in time.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
